name: Gizey
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Gizey is an unwritten tonal language. [p. 74:] Gizey is a tonal language. Experimental findings (De Dominicis 2007) demonstrate the linguistic function of two tonal registers (H and L). Particularly, the H/L tones oppose some minimal pairs both lexically and grammatically. [...] Nevertheless, field research (De Dominicis 2007) has allowed us to verify the weak functional load had by tonal oppositions in Gizey. As a consequence, it can be argued that linguistic tones in Gizey play a minor linguistic function and are probably destined to disappear, as their tonal system is endangered.
new_statements.citation: De Dominicis, Amedeo. 2008. Phonological sketch of Gizey. Studi Linguistici e Filologici Online 6: 1-78. Pisa: Dipartimento di Linguistica, Università di Pisa (ISSN 1724-5230).

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only full phonological description of Gizey treats it as a two-register (H/L) tone language with lexical and aspectual tonal contrasts of weak functional load; it contains no statement about word stress or accent at all (the words 'stress'/'accent' appear only in bibliography titles). No opened source locates a word stress in Gizey.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the sketch notes roots are maximally disyllabic (compounds, ideophones, toponyms, loans excepted) but says nothing about prominence.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology (roots, suffixed nouns, verbs) and tone; De Dominicis 2010 treats intonation-phrase prominences ('sentence stress') only as a general concept, not as a Gizey word-stress rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 gize1234 is a language-level languoid (NOCODE_Gizey) in the Masa section beside Masana [masa1322]; Glottolog also lists 'Gizay' [giza1238] as a dialect of Masana, and Ethnologue folds Gizey into Masana [mcn]. De Dominicis' data are from Djougoumta (Mayo-Danay, Guéré, Far North Cameroon; 10 speakers); Ajello 2005 and Guitang 2021 treat Gizey as a distinct language not mutually intelligible with Masa. The Masa-language audit (masa1322) had already filed De Dominicis' Gizey tone papers under Masa; they belong here.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. p. 1: 'Gizey is an unwritten tonal language.' Sec. 4 'The Tones' pp. 74-75: two tonal registers H/L, lexical minimal pairs and verbal aspect marked by tone, weak functional load, tonal system 'endangered'. 'stress'/'accent' appear only in bibliography titles. Sections: vowels/consonants, syllable structure (roots max two syllables), vowel harmony, metaphony, final vowels, tones. fetched sources from Wayback capture 2018-04-22 (journal host humnet.unipi.it dead).

sources.note: Intonation-tone interaction in a Gizey dialogue; 'stress' occurs only in a general theoretical passage on prominence (p. 2: 'Some depend also on lexical abstractions (e.g. the stress)... the tone associated with "sentence stress"'); no Gizey word-stress statement.
